security_audit.summary: Most markdown backtick and system reconnaissance detections are false positives from examples and inline documentation. The material issue is recalc.py, which installs a persistent LibreOffice Basic macro in the user profile and the skill instructs users to run it for recalculation. No prompt injection text or data exfiltration intent was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Persistent LibreOffice macro written to the user profile
remediation.suggestion: Use a temporary LibreOffice user installation directory for recalculation, remove it after execution, or require explicit user confirmation before writing to the real profile.

remediation.issue: Bundled instructions execute recalc.py without clear side-effect warning
remediation.suggestion: Document that recalc.py modifies the LibreOffice profile and explain how users can inspect, disable, or avoid that setup.

remediation.issue: External command execution depends on PATH-resolved soffice and timeout tools
remediation.suggestion: Resolve allowed executable paths explicitly, validate workbook extensions, and keep shell execution disabled for all command invocations.

- Use `data_only=True` to read calculated values: `load_workbook('file.xlsx', data_only=True)`

- Specify data types to avoid inference issues: `pd.read_excel('file.xlsx', dtype={'id': str})`
- For large files, read specific columns: `pd.read_excel('file.xlsx', usecols=['A', 'C', 'E'])`

content.value_statement: Spreadsheet work often breaks when formulas, formatting, or template conventions are changed manually. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured XLSX creation, editing, analysis, and formula validation.
actual_capabilities: Creates new Excel workbooks with formulas, formatting, sheets, and documented assumptions.
Edits existing workbooks while preserving formulas, styles, and template conventions.
Reads and analyzes spreadsheet data with pandas across one or more sheets.
Uses openpyxl for cell-level formulas, formatting, row changes, and sheet changes.
Runs recalc.py with LibreOffice to recalculate formulas and report Excel error cells.
Applies financial model conventions for colors, number formats, and source notes.
limitations: Formula recalculation requires LibreOffice to be installed and available on the system path.
The included recalc.py script writes a LibreOffice Basic macro into the user profile.
It cannot verify source data accuracy unless the user provides trusted source material.
Complex workbook macros, external links, and protected sheets may need manual review.

use_cases.description: Create forecast workbooks with formulas, assumptions, formatting, and source notes.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Workbook
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an XLSX workbook with one sheet for monthly expenses. Include category, date, amount, and a total formula.

prompt_templates.prompt: Review this spreadsheet, summarize each sheet, identify missing values, and create a cleaned workbook with the same key columns.

prompt_templates.title: Update a Template Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Update this workbook with the new assumptions. Preserve existing formulas, styles, sheet names, and number formats.

prompt_templates.title: Build and Validate a Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a three-year revenue model with assumption cells, linked formulas, source notes, formatting, and formula error validation.

output_examples.input: Create a sales summary workbook from quarterly revenue data.
output_examples.output: A workbook with raw data, a summary sheet, quarterly totals, annual totals, and formatted currency values.

output_examples.input: Check this model for formula errors after adding a new region.
output_examples.output: A validation report listing affected sheets, error types, cell locations, and recommended fixes.

output_examples.input: Convert a CSV export into a formatted Excel tracker.
output_examples.output: A clean workbook with typed columns, filters, totals, and consistent date and number formats.

best_practices: Use Excel formulas for calculated values so workbooks remain editable and dynamic.
Preserve existing workbook conventions before adding new formatting or sheets.
Run formula recalculation and review reported error cells before delivery.
anti_patterns: Do not replace formulas with static calculated values unless the user requests it.
Do not save a formula workbook after loading it with calculated values only.
Do not change established template styling without checking the existing pattern first.

faq.question: What file types does this skill support?
faq.answer: It focuses on Excel workbooks and spreadsheet data, including XLSX, XLSM, CSV, and TSV files.

faq.question: Can it preserve formulas in existing workbooks?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends openpyxl workflows that preserve formulas while editing cells, sheets, and formatting.

faq.question: Does it calculate formula results itself?
faq.answer: No. It uses LibreOffice through recalc.py to recalculate workbook formulas after changes.

faq.question: Does the recalculation script change system files?
faq.answer: It writes a LibreOffice Basic macro into the user LibreOffice profile to perform recalculation.

faq.question: Is it suitable for financial models?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for assumptions, source notes, colors, formats, and formula checks.

faq.question: Can it guarantee that workbook data is correct?
faq.answer: No. It can validate formulas and structure, but source data accuracy depends on user-provided inputs.
